segments.expected: Kellan had read about that hand in his mother's newspaper when he was eight. Everybody in Meridian had. The Proprietor's hand has not left the foundation cell since 2611. He had thought it was a figure of speech, the way the Mercury said a thing had not been out of a man's mind. Then he had sat at the long table and seen that it was not. Adlam had told him, the first night, in the street afterward: once a year, on the first of the first month, the glass was taken off its frame and cleaned by two clerks with soft cloths, and for that, and only that, the hand came up. Under a minute. Adlam had held the watch on it every year for nine years. Fifty-one seconds was the longest.

segments.expected: "You asked me," said Kellan, "to tell you what you wouldn't like to hear. On the card. Not counsel's. Yours." He did not take his eyes off his mother's watch. "Seventy years is twenty-five thousand days, and something. This is three minutes. If you lift at twenty-two, there's time. If you lift after twenty-four, there's not. If you don't lift, the low town's dry this morning, and the bank keeps your count, and the next time anything in this harbour falls into step it'll be because it was never got out, and every keeper in the country will know it was got as far as the salt and stopped because a man couldn't take his hand off a glass." He breathed.

segments.expected: Kellan felt them stop through the stone of the walk, in the soles of his boots. Six iron pumps behind the wall at his back stopped on the down-stroke and stood. The six outfalls below the landing gave one last gulp each into the hand of water on the mud, and stopped pouring. For the first time since the boat came in under the sea gate, Kellan Renn stood in Saltmere and heard nothing going four and four anywhere at all.

segments.expected: "I can't tell," said Loveday Hosken, from the south gallery, through the door. Her voice was very high and quite steady. "Mrs. Rowan. I can't tell. It's not town. It's not anything. It's so quiet I can't—" She stopped. "I can't feel my hand properly. It went when the pumps went. I've kept it on."
